Method of Attack: Trojan dropper delivering other malware strains including clicker Trojans, banking Trojans, and ransomware
Spreads using encrypted and obfuscated DEX files camouflaged as JAR archives containing compiled Android application code
DEX files decrypted and compiled using dex2oat compiler into ELF binary executed natively by device processor
Allows remote commands to be sent to the mobile device, behaving like a backdoor
Two variants: one fully stealthy (no icons or alerts), one semi-stealthy (shows notifications and icons)
Redirects victims to websites with browser games for pay-per-click profits
Attack Vector: Likely spread by web redirects via game websites or other shady websites hosted in the US
Indicators of Compromise: Malware sample hash available on VirusTotal
Domains and IP addresses used by xHelper available on VirusTotal
IP addresses hosting xHelper found in New York City, New York and Dallas, Texas
